newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan brokerages fall on lingering Nomura worries.
newsitem.headline: Japan brokerages fall on lingering Nomura worries.

text.p: Brokerage shares fell on Monday morning on lingering worries over the recent scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd and anxieties that smaller houses may not survive Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms, brokers said.

As of midday, the "Big Four" brokerages were all at new lows for the year. Nomura fell 60 yen to 1,270 with 3.358 million shares traded, making it the third most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Daiwa Securities Co Ltd shed 39 yen to 791, Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd slipped 11 yen to 324 and Nikko Securities Co Ltd fell 23 yen to 632.
Tokyo Securities Co Ltd lost 25 yen or 10.64 percent to 210, the fourth largest percentage loser. It was followed by New Japan Securities Co Ltd which was down 30 yen at 270.

"The market itself is in the doldrums and there is much speculation that the scandal concerning Nomura and 'sokaiya' racketeers will scar the industry. Private investors are opting to sell," a broker at a second-tier brokerage said.
"There are no strong reasons to hold brokerage shares at the moment, even if they are not Nomura shares," another broker said. "Dissolution of cross-shareholdings is not ceasing."
